meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_1H_2406). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: CROSSOVER BLOCK CONFIRMED: 1F q16-q26 = 1H q1-q11, eleven questions worth 40 marks. Predicted from the matching mark sequence, confirmed by reading. Coded in the same sitting as IGCSE-JUN24-F-P1; shared rows carry identical tags by construction.

GAP-CANDIDATE set_notation — q7(a)(i),(a)(ii),(b),(c), four parts, 5 marks, ALL UNTAGGED. Shared from the Foundation paper via the crossover, so this is the Higher slice's copy of the same evidence. See IGCSE-JUN24-F-P1 q22 for the full reasoning, including why venn_diagrams was rejected rather than used as an interim tag. Takes set_notation to seven parts on each slice.

GAP-CANDIDATE differentiation — q18, 5 marks, the coordinates of both points on a cubic where the gradient takes a given value. Tagged solving_quadratic_equations_factorising as an INTERIM measure, consistent with Jun25 2H q17(b): once differentiated the work is solving x squared = 16 and substituting back, which a correct answer does demonstrate. THIRD sighting.

GAP-CANDIDATE arithmetic_series_sum — q24, 6 marks. The interior angles of an n-sided polygon form an arithmetic sequence; the sum of those angles is wanted. Tagged angles_in_polygons as an INTERIM measure, which is honest and unusually good for a gap candidate — the whole method turns on equating the series sum against (n-2) x 180, so the polygon angle sum is genuinely demonstrated. THIRD sighting, and the first that is a true synthesis of the missing skill with an existing one.

GAP-CANDIDATE domain_and_range — q15(a), 1 mark, stating the value of x that cannot be in any domain of a given function. FIRST sighting of this candidate, which had zero across the first eight papers. Tagged functions_notation as an INTERIM measure: it under-claims rather than mis-claims, since the question is about the structure of a named function f, which is that skill's territory. The uncovered part is the idea of a domain and its exclusions (spec Higher 3.2 C).

q23 tagged across three volume and surface-area nodes: the route is cone volume minus hemisphere volume to find x, then the hemisphere's total surface area. The answer is a surface area but the work is mostly volume, so the volume node leads.
